name.text: Using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus with Two Variable Limits of Integration

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

We have \(F(x)=\displaystyle \int _{@lower_limit@}^{@upper_limit@}{@quest_expr@}\,dt\). Both limits of integration are variable, so we need to split this into two integrals. We get

\( \begin{align} F(x) &= \displaystyle \int _{@lower_limit@}^{@upper_limit@}{@quest_expr@}\,dt \\ &= \displaystyle \int _{@lower_limit@}^{0}{@quest_expr@}\,dt +\int _{0}^{@upper_limit@}{@quest_expr@}\,dt\\ &=-\displaystyle \int _{@lower_limit@}^{0}{@quest_expr@}\,dt+\int _{0}^{@upper_limit@}{@quest_expr@}\,dt\\ \end{align} \)

Differentiating the first term, we obtain

\(\frac{d}{dx} \left [ \displaystyle -\int_{0}^{@lower_limit@}{@quest_expr@} \right ]={@soln1@}\)

Differentiating the second term, we first let \(u(x)=2x\). Then,

\( \begin{align} \frac{d}{dx} \left [ \displaystyle \int _{0}^{@upper_limit@} {@quest_expr@}\,dt \right ] &= \frac{d}{dx} \left [ \displaystyle \int _{0}^{u(x)}{@quest_expr@}\,dt \right ]\\ &=(u(x))^{@power@}.\frac{du}{dx}\\ &=({@upper_limit@})^{@power@}.{2}\\ &={@soln2@}\\ \end{align} \)

Thus,

\( \begin{align} F'(x) &= \frac{d}{dx} \left [\displaystyle -\int_{0}^{@lower_limit@}{@quest_expr@}\,dt +\right ]+\frac{d}{dx}\left [\displaystyle -\int_{0}^{@upper_limit@}{@quest_expr@}\,dt \right ]\displaystyle \\ &= \displaystyle {@ta@}\\ &={@soln1@}+{@soln2@}\\ &={@ta@}\\ \end{align} \)
